stem: A solutions architect converts a stated limit of about 53 minutes of downtime per year into the correct metric and target for a service level agreement. Which is it?

choices.text: An availability target of 99.9% for the same annual downtime budget.

rationale: An annual downtime budget of about 53 minutes corresponds to 99.99% availability, since that is the uptime percentage that leaves roughly that amount of downtime across a full year. 99.9% availability corresponds to roughly 8.8 hours of downtime a year, which is far more downtime than the stated 53-minute limit allows. An RTO measures how long a specific workload may stay down after a disruption before it must be back, not the total downtime budget across an entire year, so it is the wrong metric for this stated limit. An RPO measures how much data may be lost, not how much downtime is acceptable, so it does not match a downtime figure at all.
